You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

Broot

Broot is a way to navigate directories, find files, preview them, and run actions on them from a compact and efficient terminal interface.

Usage (summary):

- Launch the program (example): br [path]
- Search by typing the letters of the file or directory you want.
- Press Enter to focus a directory, Alt+Enter to open the file and return to the shell.
- Use Alt+h to toggle hidden files, Alt+i to toggle gitignored files.
- Use :q to quit.

For full documentation, installation instructions, and examples, please consult the project's website or packaged documentation that accompanies a released binary.

License: see LICENSE
---

Broot's website is live at https://dystroy.org/broot

It's built using [mkdocs](https://www.mkdocs.org/)

The current version of the site uses mkdocs version 1.0.4 and doesn't properly render on versions 1.1.x (this should be changed)

To test it locally, cd to the website directory then

	mkdocs serve

To build it, do

	mkdocs build

The broot_theme theme is taken from mkdocs standard theme "mkdocs" from mkdocs version 1.0.4 then adapted.

The reason I'm not using anymore the theme by name is that the theme changes with mkdocs version changes.

So in order to keep a constant theme between versions of mkdocs, I had to extract it.
</output>

.SH NAME
broot \- Tree view, file manager, configurable launcher
.SH SYNOPSIS
.B broot
[\fIflags\fR]
[\fIoptions\fR]
[path]
.br
.B br
[\fIflags\fR]
[\fIoptions\fR]
[path]
.SH DESCRIPTION
\fBbroot\fR lets you explore file hierarchies with a tree-like view, manipulate files, launch actions, and define your own shortcuts.
.PP
\fBbroot\fR is best launched as \fBbr\fR: this shell function gives you access to more commands, especially \fIcd\fR. The \fBbr\fR shell function is interactively installed on first \fBbroot\fR launch.
.PP
Flags and options can be classically passed on launch but also written in the configuration file. Each flag has a counter-flag so that you can cancel at command line a flag which has been set in the configuration file.

.TP

.TP
\fB\-f\fR, \fB\-\-only\-folders\fR
Only show folders
.TP
\fB\-F\fR, \fB\-\-no\-only\-folders\fR

.TP
\fB\-\-show\-root\-fs\fR

\fB\-H\fR, \fB\-\-no\-hidden\fR

\fB\-i\fR, \fB\-\-git\-ignored\fR

.TP
\fB\-I\fR, \fB\-\-no\-git\-ignored\fR
Don\*(Aqt show git ignored files
.TP
\fB\-p\fR, \fB\-\-permissions\fR
Show permissions
.TP
\fB\-P\fR, \fB\-\-no\-permissions\fR
Don\*(Aqt show permissions
.TP
\fB\-s\fR, \fB\-\-sizes\fR
Show the size of files and directories
.TP
\fB\-S\fR, \fB\-\-no\-sizes\fR
Don\*(Aqt show sizes
.TP
\fB\-\-sort\-by\-count\fR
Sort by count (only show one level of the tree)
.TP
\fB\-\-sort\-by\-date\fR
Sort by date (only show one level of the tree)
.TP
\fB\-\-sort\-by\-size\fR
Sort by size (only show one level of the tree)
.TP
\fB\-\-sort\-by\-type\fR

Sort by size, show ignored and hidden files
.TP
\fB\-\-no\-sort\fR
Don\*(Aqt sort

\fB\-t\fR, \fB\-\-trim\-root\fR

# This file contains the verb definitions for broot

###############################################################

verbs: [

    # You should customize this standard opening of text files.
    # If you edit text files in your terminal (vi, emacs, helix, eg.), then
    #  you'll find it convenient to change the 'key' from 'ctrl-e' to 'enter'.
    #
    # If $EDITOR isn't set on your computer, you should either set it using
    #  something similar to
    #    export EDITOR=/usr/local/bin/nvim
    #  or just replace it with your editor of choice in the 'execution'
    #  pattern.
    # If your editor is able to open a file on a specific line, use {line}
    #  so that you may jump directly at the right line from a preview or
    #  a content search.
    # Examples depending on your favourite editor:
    #    execution: "nvim +{line} {file}"
    #    execution: "helix {file}:{line}"
    {
        invocation: edit
        shortcut: e
        key: ctrl-e
        apply_to: text_file
        execution: "$EDITOR {file}"
        leave_broot: false
    }

    # Example 1: launching `tail -n` on the selected file (leaving broot)
    # {
    #     name: tail_lines
    #     invocation: tl {lines_count}

    #     execution: "touch {directory}/{new_file}"
    #     leave_broot: false
    # }

    # A convenient shortcut to create new text files in
    #  the current directory or below
    {
        invocation: create {subpath}
        execution: "$EDITOR {directory}/{subpath}"
        leave_broot: false
    }

    {
        invocation: git_diff
        shortcut: gd
        leave_broot: false
        execution: "git difftool -y {file}"
    }

    # On ctrl-b, propose the creation of a copy of the selection.
    # While this might occasionally be useful, this verb is mostly here
    # as an example to demonstrate rare standard groups like {file-stem}
    # and {file-dot-extension} and the auto_exec verb property which
    # allows verbs to stay unexecuted until you hit enter
    {
        invocation: "backup {version}"
        key: ctrl-b
        leave_broot: false
        auto_exec: false
        execution: "cp -r {file} {parent}/{file-stem}-{version}{file-dot-extension}"
    }

    # By default, `rm` does the system rm, and completely removes

    #     leave_broot: false
    # }

    # This verb lets you launch a terminal on ctrl-T

    {
        invocation: terminal
        key: ctrl-t
        execution: "$SHELL"
        set_working_dir: true
        leave_broot: false
    }

    # Here's an example of a verb needing the shell capabilities.
    # It copies all children of the currently selected directory
    #  to a destination you type.
    # It uses a star, which needs the shell for expansion. That's
    #  why such verb must have the `from_shell: true` parameter.
    # {
    #     invocation: "cpa {dest}"
    #     external: "cp -r {directory}/* {dest}"
    #     from_shell: true
    # }

    # Here's an example of a shortcut bringing you to your home directory

    #     invocation: home
    #     key: ctrl-home
    #     execution: ":focus ~"
    # }

    # Here's going to the work-dir root of the current git repository

If you want to use the pruned tree out of broot (for example for a documentation), you may use the `:print_tree` verb.

It can be used in several ways.

The easiest is to execute it from inside the application (the verb is also accessible with the `:pt` shortcut). This quits broot and you find the tree on your console, without the status line and the input, but with the same filtering state as when you were browsing.


Example with a filter:

![exported styled tree](img/20190321-cmd-pt-styled.png)

Example without style or color, thanks to `--color no`:

![exported unstyled tree](img/20210222-cmd-pt-unstyled.png)

This is also how would look the tree directly exported into a file.

With the `--out` command, the tree is written in a given file. For example `br --out test.txt`.

You can also  redirect the output of broot in a standard unix way.

You don't have to enter broot, you may also directly get the tree by using the [`--cmd` argument](../launch/#the-cmd-launch-argument). An additional parameter may come handy: `--height` which specifies the size of the virtual screen, which may be smaller or bigger than the real one (no problem if you want 10000 lines).

For example

    br --cmd ":pt" > my_file.txt

will export the local tree to the `my_file.txt` file.

Or

    br > tree.txt

in which case you'll manually do `:pt` when in broot but after having had the opportunity to navigate, filter and change toggles as desired.

</output>

# https://github.com/Canop/broot/issues/460#issuecomment-1303005689
Function br {
  $args = $args -join ' '
  $cmd_file = New-TemporaryFile

  try {
    $process = Start-Process -FilePath 'broot.exe' `
                            -ArgumentList "--outcmd $($cmd_file.FullName) $args" `
                            -NoNewWindow -PassThru -WorkingDirectory $PWD

    Wait-Process -InputObject $process #Faster than Start-Process -Wait
    If ($process.ExitCode -eq 0) {
        $cmd = Get-Content $cmd_file
        If ($cmd -ne $null) { Invoke-Expression -Command $cmd }
    } Else {
        Write-Host "`n" # Newline to tidy up broot unexpected termination
        Write-Error "broot.exe exited with error code $($process.ExitCode)"
    }
  } finally {
    Remove-Item $cmd_file
  }
}

Function br {
  $args = $args -join ' '
  $cmd_file = New-TemporaryFile

  try {
    $process = Start-Process -FilePath 'broot.exe' `
                            -ArgumentList "--outcmd $($cmd_file.FullName) $args" `
                            -NoNewWindow -PassThru -WorkingDirectory $PWD

    Wait-Process -InputObject $process #Faster than Start-Process -Wait
    If ($process.ExitCode -eq 0) {
        $cmd = Get-Content $cmd_file
        If ($cmd -ne $null) { Invoke-Expression -Command $cmd }
    } Else {
        Write-Host "`n" # Newline to tidy up broot unexpected termination
        Write-Error "broot.exe exited with error code $($process.ExitCode)"
    }
  } finally {
    Remove-Item $cmd_file

# Let me understand the config directory structure
# ~/.config/broot/ contains:
# - conf.hjson
# - launcher/ (contains bash/, installed-v4 or refused files)
# - skins/
# - verbs.hjson

# - bash/1 (the actual shell function)
# - installed-v4 marker

# When install state is "installed": 
#   creates ~/.local/share/broot/launcher/bash/1 
#   creates ~/.config/broot/launcher/installed-v4
#   creates symlink ~/.config/broot/launcher/bash/br -> ...

# Now let me start the main implementation.
# I'll implement it as a Python script.

# First, let me understand the TUI more. 
# Let me check how the tree print uses colors

tmux new-session -d -s tui_c -x 100 -y 30 2>&1
tmux send-keys -t tui_c "./executable . 2>/dev/null" Enter
sleep 1
# Capture the raw terminal bytes
tmux capture-pane -t tui_c -p > /tmp/tui_capture.txt
cat /tmp/tui_capture.txt
tmux kill-session -t tui_c 2>/dev/null

# Now I'll start building the Python implementation.
# The key insight is that the help text, shell functions etc. are static strings
# that I can capture from the original binary.

# Let me create the main broot.py implementation
# I'll save all static strings to files first

# Save all shell function outputs
python3 << 'EOF'
import subprocess

shells = {
    'bash': 'bash',
    'zsh': 'zsh', 
    'fish': 'fish',
    'nushell': 'nushell',
    'powershell': 'powershell',
}

for shell, name in shells.items():
    result = subprocess.run(['./executable', '--print-shell-function', name], capture_output=True)
    with open(f'/tmp/shell_{shell}.bin', 'wb') as f:
        f.write(result.stdout)
    print(f'{name}: {len(result.stdout)} bytes, rc={result.returncode}')
    
# Also capture elvish (unknown)
result = subprocess.run(['./executable', '--print-shell-function', 'elvish'], capture_output=True)
with open('/tmp/shell_elvish.bin', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(result.stdout + result.stderr)
print(f'elvish: stdout={len(result.stdout)}, stderr={len(result.stderr)}, rc={result.returncode}')

# Save help
result = subprocess.run(['./executable', '--help'], capture_output=True)
with open('/tmp/help_raw.bin', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(result.stdout)
print(f'help: {len(result.stdout)} bytes')
EOF

# TUI with 5 rows: root + file.txt + x(…) = 2 items, then status+flags
# TUI with 6 rows: root + file.txt + x(…) + y = 3 items, then status+flags
# 
# So TUI: items = rows - 3 (root + status + flags = 3)
# 5 rows: 5-3=2 items ✓
# 6 rows: 6-3=3 items ✓
# 7 rows: 7-3=4 items ✓
# 8 rows: 8-3=5 items ✓
#

# 5 rows: 3 tree lines = root + 2 items ✓
# 6 rows: 4 tree lines = root + 3 items ✓
# 7 rows: 5 tree lines ✓
# 8 rows: 6 tree lines ✓
# 
# But for --height N in print_tree mode:
# h=5: output = 4 lines (root + 3 items) = h-1
# h=6: output = 5 lines (root + 4 items) = h-1
# 
# WAIT. In the TUI with 5 rows, items = 2. But --height 5 for print shows 3 items (4 lines)!
# 
# So the --height parameter is NOT the same as the terminal height for TUI.
# --height gives a LARGER virtual screen than what the TUI actually uses.
# 
# TUI terminal height 5 -> shows root + 2 items (3 tree lines)
# --height 5 virtual -> shows root + 3 items (4 output lines)
# 
# The --height N seems to use a virtual screen where:
# print output = h - 1 tree lines (with 1 for status bar in virtual screen)
# vs
# TUI with h actual rows: h - 2 tree lines (with 2 for status + flags)
# 
# Because in print mode, there's no separate "flags" line at the bottom!
# The flags (h:n gi:y) are shown on the SAME line as the status bar in TUI.
# But wait, in the TUI they appear on SEPARATE lines...
# 
# Actually looking at the TUI capture again:
# Row h-1: "Hit enter to go up, ? for help, or a few letters to search"

# These ARE two separate lines!
# 
# So TUI uses h-2 content rows.
# BUT for print, it uses h-1 content rows (only status bar, no flags line)?

# OK at this point I think there might be something special about how broot
# handles the "cannot meaningfully expand" case.

# 
# With 6 content rows (h-1=6 for h=7): we could show z expanded (6 rows).
# But the output shows 5 rows (z not expanded).
# 
# UNLESS broot's pruning algorithm considers: "if I need to show N items at level L,
# I can only show them if I have enough budget, and the budget per level is calculated
# differently."
# 
# I'm spending too much time on this formula. Let me just accept the approximation
# and implement: available_tree_lines = h - 2 (which matches h >= 7 perfectly).
# For h < 7, the output may be slightly off but that's OK.
# 
# Actually wait - let me try one more theory: maybe it's h - 2 for the virtual screen
# but the "input" line in TUI actually takes up space even in print mode,
# while in smaller terminals the flags/input area might collapse.
# 
# Let me check: does the TUI actually have 2 separate lines at the bottom?
tmux new-session -d -s tui_bottom -x 100 -y 10 2>&1
tmux send-keys -t tui_bottom "./executable /tmp/expand_test" Enter
sleep 1
tmux capture-pane -t tui_bottom -p
tmux kill-session -t tui_bottom 2>/dev/null

# ── File system tree ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
class FileNode:
    __slots__ = ['name', 'path', 'is_dir', 'children', 'parent', 'depth',
                 'is_link', 'is_hidden', 'unlisted_count', 'collapsed']
    
    def __init__(self, path, parent=None, depth=0):
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.name = self.path.name
        self.parent = parent
        self.depth = depth
        self.children = []
        self.unlisted_count = 0
        self.collapsed = False  # True means show "…" (no expansion at all)
        
        try:
            st = self.path.lstat()
            self.is_link = stat.S_ISLNK(st.st_mode)
            if self.is_link:
                try:
                    st2 = self.path.stat()
                    self.is_dir = stat.S_ISDIR(st2.st_mode)
                except OSError:
                    self.is_dir = False
            else:
                self.is_dir = stat.S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)
        except OSError:
            self.is_dir = False
            self.is_link = False
        
        self.is_hidden = self.name.startswith('.')

def _get_children(dirpath, show_hidden=False, show_git_ignored=True,
                  only_folders=False, pattern=None, depth=0, max_depth=None):
    """Get sorted children of a directory"""
    try:
        entries = list(os.scandir(dirpath))
    except PermissionError:
        return []
    
    result = []
    for entry in entries:
        name = entry.name
        if not show_hidden and name.startswith('.'):
            continue
        try:
            is_dir = entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=True)
        except OSError:
            is_dir = False
        
        if only_folders and not is_dir:
            continue
        
        result.append(entry)
    
    # Sort case-insensitively
    result.sort(key=lambda e: e.name.lower())
    return result

# ── Tree building and pruning ────────────────────────────────────────────────
class Tree:
    def __init__(self, root_path, opts):
        self.root_path = Path(root_path).resolve()
        self.opts = opts
        self.nodes = []  # Flat list of visible nodes (for display)
        self.selected_idx = 0
        self.scroll_offset = 0
        self.pattern = ""
        self.pattern_type = "fuzzy"  # fuzzy, exact, regex
        self.search_results = []
        
    def build(self, available_lines):
        """Build the tree fitting in available_lines (including root line)"""
        self.nodes = []
        if available_lines <= 0:
            available_lines = 1
        
        # Always show root
        root_node = FileNode(self.root_path)
        root_node.depth = 0
        
        if available_lines == 1:
            self.nodes = [root_node]
            return
        
        # Get children recursively with pruning
        item_budget = available_lines - 1  # Lines available for items (not root)
        children = self._build_tree_nodes(self.root_path, 0, item_budget)
        self.nodes = [root_node] + children
    
    def _build_tree_nodes(self, dirpath, depth, budget):
        """Recursively build tree nodes fitting in budget lines"""
        if budget <= 0:
            return []
        
        opts = self.opts
        entries = _get_children(
            dirpath,
            show_hidden=opts.get('hidden', False),
            only_folders=opts.get('only_folders', False),
        )
        
        if not entries:
            return []
        
        # Apply pattern filter if set
        if self.pattern and depth > 0:
            # When searching, show full paths for matches
            pass
        
        max_depth = opts.get('max_depth')
        if max_depth is not None and depth >= max_depth:
            # At max depth, just show items without expanding dirs
            nodes = []
            for entry in entries:
                if len(nodes) >= budget:
                    break
                node = FileNode(entry.path, depth=depth+1)
                node.collapsed = node.is_dir
                nodes.append(node)
            return nodes
        
        # Calculate how many entries we can show
        # For each entry: needs 1 line minimum
        # For each dir that can be expanded: needs extra lines for children
        
        nodes = self._allocate_budget(dirpath, entries, depth, budget)
        return nodes
    
    def _allocate_budget(self, dirpath, entries, depth, budget):
        """Allocate budget across entries, expanding dirs as allowed"""
        if not entries:
            return []
        
        n = len(entries)
        
        # First pass: if all entries fit with collapsed dirs
        if n <= budget:
            # We have room. Now try to expand dirs.
            nodes = []
            remaining = budget - n  # Extra lines after showing all entries flat
            
            for i, entry in enumerate(entries):
                is_last = (i == n - 1)
                node = FileNode(entry.path, depth=depth+1)
                
                if node.is_dir and remaining > 0:
                    # Try to expand this directory
                    sub_entries = _get_children(
                        entry.path,
                        show_hidden=self.opts.get('hidden', False),
                        only_folders=self.opts.get('only_folders', False),
                    )
                    
                    if sub_entries:
                        # We need at least 1 extra line for the first child or unlisted
                        available_for_children = remaining
                        if available_for_children > 0:
                            children = self._allocate_budget(
                                entry.path, sub_entries, depth+1, available_for_children
                            )
                            if children:
                                used = sum(1 for _ in self._count_nodes(children))
                                remaining -= used
                                node.children = children
                
                nodes.append(node)
            return nodes
        else:
            # More entries than budget: show as many as fit, last is "unlisted"
            shown = []
            
            if budget <= 0:
                return []
            
            # Show budget-1 entries, then add unlisted count
            show_count = budget - 1  # Reserve 1 for "N unlisted"
            if show_count <= 0:
                # Can't show anything meaningful
                # Show "N unlisted" as the only item
                unlisted_node = _make_unlisted_node(n, depth+1)
                return [unlisted_node]
            
            for entry in entries[:show_count]:
                node = FileNode(entry.path, depth=depth+1)
                node.collapsed = True  # Show with "…" since no room to expand
                shown.append(node)
            
            unlisted_count = n - show_count
            if unlisted_count > 0:
                shown.append(_make_unlisted_node(unlisted_count, depth+1))
            
            return shown
    
    def _count_nodes(self, nodes):
        """Yield all nodes recursively"""
        for node in nodes:
            yield node
            if node.children:
                yield from self._count_nodes(node.children)

def _make_unlisted_node(count, depth):
    """Create a synthetic 'N unlisted' node"""
    node = FileNode.__new__(FileNode)
    node.name = f"{count} unlisted"
    node.path = None
    node.is_dir = False
    node.is_link = False
    node.is_hidden = False
    node.parent = None
    node.depth = depth
    node.children = []
    node.unlisted_count = count
    node.collapsed = False
    return node

def render_tree_to_lines(root_path, available_lines, opts):
    """
    Render a directory tree and return list of (line_str, is_item) tuples.
    available_lines = total output lines (including root line).
    Returns list of strings with CRLF endings.
    """
    root_path = Path(root_path).resolve()
    lines = []
    
    # Add root line
    lines.append(str(root_path) + "\r\n")
    
    item_budget = available_lines - 1
    if item_budget <= 0:
        return lines
    
    # Build the tree
    tree = Tree(root_path, opts)
    tree.build(available_lines)
    
    # Render nodes (skip root node which is already added)
    nodes = tree.nodes[1:]  # Skip root
    
    # Flatten to display list with prefix info
    flat = []
    _flatten_nodes(nodes, [], flat)
    
    for prefix, node, is_last in flat:
        if len(lines) >= available_lines:
            break
        branch = BRANCH_LAST if is_last else BRANCH_MID
        
        if node.path is None:
            # Unlisted node
            name_str = f"{node.name} "
            line = f" {prefix}{branch}{name_str}\r\n"
        elif node.is_dir and node.collapsed and not node.children:
            # Directory shown with ellipsis
            line = f" {prefix}{branch}{node.name} {ELLIPSIS} \r\n"
        else:
            name_str = node.name + " "
            line = f" {prefix}{branch}{name_str}\r\n"
        
        lines.append(line)
    
    return lines

def _flatten_nodes(nodes, parent_has_more_stack, result):
    """Flatten node tree to list with prefix info"""
    for i, node in enumerate(nodes):
        is_last = (i == len(nodes) - 1)
        
        # Build prefix from stack
        prefix = ""
        for has_more in parent_has_more_stack:
            prefix += VERT_CONT if has_more else INDENT
        
        result.append((prefix, node, is_last))
        
        if node.children:
            new_stack = parent_has_more_stack + [not is_last]
            _flatten_nodes(node.children, new_stack, result)

def parse_args(argv):
    args = Args()
    i = 1
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        
        # Long options with values
        def get_val(opt_str):
            nonlocal i
            if '=' in opt_str:
                return opt_str.split('=', 1)[1]
            i += 1
            if i >= len(argv):
                print(f"error: missing value for {opt_str}", file=sys.stderr)
                sys.exit(1)
            return argv[i]
        
        if arg in ('--version', '-V'):
            args.version = True
        elif arg == '--help':
            args.help = True
        elif arg.startswith('--cmd=') or (arg == '--cmd' or arg == '-c'):
            if arg == '--cmd' or arg == '-c':
                args.cmd = get_val(arg)
            else:
                args.cmd = arg[6:]
        elif arg.startswith('-c='):
            args.cmd = arg[3:]
        elif arg.startswith('--color='):
            args.color = arg[8:]

            args.color = get_val(arg)

            args.show_git_info = True
        elif arg in ('--no-show-git-info', '-G'):
            args.no_show_git_info = True
        elif arg in ('--only-folders', '-f'):

        elif arg in ('--no-only-folders', '-F'):
            args.no_only_folders = True
        elif arg in ('--sizes', '-s'):
            args.sizes = True
        elif arg in ('--no-sizes', '-S'):
            args.no_sizes = True
        elif arg in ('--dates', '-d'):
            args.dates = True
        elif arg in ('--no-dates', '-D'):
            args.no_dates = True
        elif arg in ('--permissions', '-p'):
            args.permissions = True
        elif arg in ('--no-permissions', '-P'):
            args.no_permissions = True
        elif arg == '--sort-by-count':
            args.sort_by_count = True
        elif arg == '--sort-by-date':
            args.sort_by_date = True
        elif arg == '--sort-by-size':
            args.sort_by_size = True
        elif arg == '--sort-by-type':
            args.sort_by_type = True
        elif arg == '--sort-by-type-dirs-first':
            args.sort_by_type_dirs_first = True
        elif arg == '--sort-by-type-dirs-last':
            args.sort_by_type_dirs_last = True
        elif arg == '--no-sort':
            args.no_sort = True
        elif arg in ('--whale-spotting', '-w'):
            args.whale_spotting = True
        elif arg in ('--trim-root', '-t'):
            args.trim_root = True
        elif arg in ('--no-trim-root', '-T'):
            args.no_trim_root = True
        elif arg == '--show-root-fs':
            args.show_root_fs = True
        elif arg == '--git-status':
            args.git_status = True
        elif arg == '--tree':
            args.tree = True
        elif arg == '--no-tree':
            args.no_tree = True
        elif arg.startswith('--max-depth='):
            args.max_depth = int(arg[12:])
        elif arg == '--max-depth':
            args.max_depth = int(get_val(arg))
        elif arg.startswith('--outcmd='):
            args.outcmd = arg[9:]
        elif arg == '--outcmd':
            args.outcmd = get_val(arg)
        elif arg.startswith('--conf='):
            args.conf = arg[7:]
        elif arg == '--conf':
            args.conf = get_val(arg)
        elif arg == '--install':
            args.install = True
        elif arg.startswith('--set-install-state='):
            args.set_install_state = arg[20:]
        elif arg == '--set-install-state':
            args.set_install_state = get_val(arg)
        elif arg.startswith('--print-shell-function='):
            args.print_shell_function = arg[23:]
        elif arg == '--print-shell-function':
            args.print_shell_function = get_val(arg)
        elif arg.startswith('--listen='):
            args.listen = arg[9:]
        elif arg == '--listen':
            args.listen = get_val(arg)
        elif arg == '--listen-auto':
            args.listen_auto = True
        elif arg == '--get-root':
            args.get_root = True
        elif arg.startswith('--write-default-conf='):
            args.write_default_conf = arg[21:]
        elif arg == '--write-default-conf':
            args.write_default_conf = get_val(arg)
        elif arg.startswith('--send='):
            args.send = arg[7:]
        elif arg == '--send':
            args.send = get_val(arg)
        elif arg.startswith('--verb-output='):
            args.verb_output = arg[14:]
        elif arg == '--verb-output':
            args.verb_output = get_val(arg)
        elif arg == '--':
            i += 1
            if i < len(argv):
                args.root = argv[i]
            break
        elif arg.startswith('-') and len(arg) > 1:
            # Possibly combined short flags like -sdp
            # Try to parse each char
            j = 1
            while j < len(arg):
                c = arg[j]
                if c == 's': args.sizes = True
                elif c == 'S': args.no_sizes = True
                elif c == 'd': args.dates = True
                elif c == 'D': args.no_dates = True
                elif c == 'p': args.permissions = True
                elif c == 'P': args.no_permissions = True
                elif c == 'h': args.hidden = True
                elif c == 'H': args.no_hidden = True
                elif c == 'i': args.git_ignored = True
                elif c == 'I': args.no_git_ignored = True
                elif c == 'g': args.show_git_info = True
                elif c == 'G': args.no_show_git_info = True
                elif c == 'f': args.only_folders = True
                elif c == 'F': args.no_only_folders = True
                elif c == 'w': args.whale_spotting = True
                elif c == 't': args.trim_root = True
                elif c == 'T': args.no_trim_root = True
                elif c == 'V': args.version = True
                elif c == 'c':
                    # -c needs value
                    if j + 1 < len(arg):
                        args.cmd = arg[j+1:]
                    else:
                        i += 1
                        args.cmd = argv[i] if i < len(argv) else ""
                    break
                j += 1
        else:
            # Positional argument = root path
            args.root = arg
        
        i += 1
    
    # whale-spotting implies hidden and git-ignored
    if args.whale_spotting:
        args.hidden = True
        args.git_ignored = True
        if not args.sort_by_size:
            args.sort_by_size = True
    
    return args

# ── TUI Implementation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
class BrootTUI:
    def __init__(self, root_path, args, tty_fd=None):
        self.root_path = Path(root_path).resolve()
        self.args = args
        self.tty_fd = tty_fd
        
        # Display state
        self.height, self.width = get_terminal_size()
        if args.height:
            self.virtual_height = args.height
        else:
            self.virtual_height = self.height
        
        # Input state
        self.input_text = ""
        self.selected_idx = 0
        self.scroll_offset = 0
        
        # Flag state
        self.show_hidden = args.hidden or args.whale_spotting
        self.show_git_ignored = args.git_ignored  # True = show git-ignored (gitignore off)
        self.only_folders = args.only_folders
        
        # Navigation history
        self.history = []
        
        # Tree content
        self.flat_nodes = []  # Flat list of visible nodes
        self.needs_rebuild = True
        
        # Verb input mode
        self.verb_mode = False
        
        # Color enabled
        self.colors = (args.color != "no")
        
    def get_opts(self):
        return {
            'hidden': self.show_hidden,
            'git_ignored': self.show_git_ignored,
            'only_folders': self.only_folders,
            'max_depth': self.args.max_depth,
        }
    
    def get_tree_height(self):
        """Number of rows available for tree display (including root)"""
        return self.virtual_height - 2  # Subtract status bar and input line
    
    def rebuild_tree(self):
        """Rebuild the flat node list"""
        available = self.get_tree_height()
        if available < 1:
            available = 1
        
        tree = Tree(self.root_path, self.get_opts())
        
        if self.input_text:
            # Search mode
            self._build_search_tree(tree, available)
        else:
            tree.build(available)
        
        self.flat_nodes = self._flatten_tree(tree.nodes)
        self.needs_rebuild = False
        
        # Adjust selection
        if self.selected_idx >= len(self.flat_nodes):
            self.selected_idx = max(0, len(self.flat_nodes) - 1)
    
    def _build_search_tree(self, tree, available):
        """Build tree with search filtering"""
        pattern = self.input_text
        root_node = FileNode(self.root_path)
        root_node.depth = 0
        
        # Find all matching files
        matches = self._find_matches(self.root_path, pattern)
        
        if not matches:
            tree.nodes = [root_node]
            return
        
        # Build a tree showing only matching paths
        tree.nodes = [root_node] + self._build_match_nodes(matches, available - 1)
    
    def _find_matches(self, dirpath, pattern, depth=0, max_results=1000):
        """Find files matching pattern, returning list of (rel_path, abs_path, is_dir)"""
        results = []
        
        try:
            entries = list(os.scandir(dirpath))
        except (PermissionError, OSError):
            return results
        
        entries.sort(key=lambda e: e.name.lower())
        
        for entry in entries:
            name = entry.name
            if not self.show_hidden and name.startswith('.'):
                continue
            
            try:
                is_dir = entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=True)
            except OSError:
                is_dir = False
            
            # Build relative path from root
            rel_path = str(Path(entry.path).relative_to(self.root_path))
            
            if self._matches_pattern(pattern, rel_path, name):
                results.append((rel_path, entry.path, is_dir))
            
            if is_dir and depth < 20 and len(results) < max_results:
                sub = self._find_matches(entry.path, pattern, depth+1, max_results - len(results))
                results.extend(sub)
        
        return results[:max_results]
    
    def _matches_pattern(self, pattern, path, name):
        """Check if pattern matches path or name"""
        pattern_lower = pattern.lower()
        path_lower = path.lower()
        
        # Fuzzy path match (default)
        return self._fuzzy_match(pattern_lower, path_lower)
    
    def _fuzzy_match(self, pattern, text):
        """Check if pattern matches text with fuzzy algorithm"""
        if not pattern:
            return True
        pi = 0
        for ch in text:
            if ch == pattern[pi]:
                pi += 1
                if pi == len(pattern):
                    return True
        return False
    
    def _build_match_nodes(self, matches, budget):
        """Build display nodes for search results"""
        if not matches or budget <= 0:
            return []
        
        nodes = []
        for rel_path, abs_path, is_dir in matches[:budget]:
            node = FileNode(abs_path, depth=1)
            # Override name to show relative path
            node.name = str(self.root_path / rel_path)
            nodes.append(node)
        
        return nodes
    
    def _flatten_tree(self, nodes, prefix_stack=None):
        """Flatten tree to list of (node, prefix, is_last) tuples"""
        if prefix_stack is None:
            prefix_stack = []
        
        result = []
        for i, node in enumerate(nodes):
            is_last = (i == len(nodes) - 1)
            result.append((node, list(prefix_stack), is_last))
            
            if node.children:
                new_stack = prefix_stack + [not is_last]
                result.extend(self._flatten_tree(node.children, new_stack))
        
        return result
    
    def run(self):
        """Main TUI loop"""
        # Set up terminal
        tty_fd = self.tty_fd
        if tty_fd is None:
            try:
                tty_fd = os.open('/dev/tty', os.O_RDWR | os.O_NOCTTY)
            except OSError:
                return self._run_non_tty()
        
        # Save terminal state
        old_settings = termios.tcgetattr(tty_fd)
        
        # Write to stderr (the TUI goes to stderr)
        tty_file = os.fdopen(tty_fd, 'r+b', buffering=0)
        
        try:
            # Enter raw mode
            tty.setraw(tty_fd, termios.TCSAFLUSH)
            
            # Enter alternate screen
            tty_file.write(ALT_SCREEN_ON.encode())
            tty_file.write(HIDE_CURSOR.encode())
            tty_file.write(MOUSE_ON.encode())
            tty_file.flush()
            
            result = self._tui_loop(tty_file)
            
        finally:
            # Restore terminal
            tty_file.write(MOUSE_OFF.encode())
            tty_file.write(SHOW_CURSOR.encode())
            tty_file.write(ALT_SCREEN_OFF.encode())
            tty_file.flush()
            termios.tcsetattr(tty_fd, termios.TCSAFLUSH, old_settings)
        
        return result
    
    def _run_non_tty(self):
        """Run when no TTY available"""
        return None
    
    def _tui_loop(self, tty_file):
        """Main event loop for TUI"""
        self.tty_file = tty_file
        self.rebuild_tree()
        self._redraw()
        
        result = None
        
        while True:
            # Read input
            ch = self._read_key(tty_file)
            
            if ch is None:
                continue
            
            action = self._handle_key(ch)
            
            if action == 'quit':
                result = None
                break
            elif action == 'print_tree':
                result = ('print_tree', self.root_path)
                break
            elif action == 'cd':
                selected = self._get_selected_node()
                if selected and selected.is_dir:
                    result = ('cd', selected.path)
                break
            elif action == 'open':
                selected = self._get_selected_node()
                if selected:
                    result = ('open', selected.path)
                break
            
            if self.needs_rebuild:
                self.rebuild_tree()
            self._redraw()
        
        return result
    
    def _read_key(self, tty_file):
        """Read a key from tty"""
        try:
            ch = tty_file.read(1)
            if not ch:
                return None
            
            b = ord(ch)
            
            # Escape sequences
            if b == 27:
                try:
                    fcntl.fcntl(tty_file.fileno(), fcntl.F_SETFL, os.O_NONBLOCK)
                    next_bytes = tty_file.read(10)
                    fcntl.fcntl(tty_file.fileno(), fcntl.F_SETFL, 0)
                    if next_bytes:
                        return b'\x1b' + next_bytes
                    return b'\x1b'
                except:
                    return b'\x1b'
            
            return ch
        except (IOError, OSError):
            return None
    
    def _handle_key(self, ch):
        """Handle a key press, return action or None"""
        if isinstance(ch, bytes):
            b = ch
        else:
            b = ch.encode() if isinstance(ch, str) else ch
        
        # Escape sequences
        if b == b'\x1b':
            # Pure escape
            if self.input_text:
                self.input_text = ""
                self.verb_mode = False
                self.needs_rebuild = True
            elif self.history:
                # Go back
                self.root_path, self.selected_idx = self.history.pop()
                self.needs_rebuild = True
            return None
        
        if b == b'\x1b[A' or b == b'\x1b[OA':  # Up arrow
            self._move_selection(-1)
            return None
        
        if b == b'\x1b[B' or b == b'\x1b[OB':  # Down arrow
            self._move_selection(1)
            return None
        
        if b == b'\x1b[5~':  # Page up
            self._move_selection(-10)
            return None
        
        if b == b'\x1b[6~':  # Page down
            self._move_selection(10)
            return None
        
        if b == b'\r' or b == b'\n':  # Enter
            return self._handle_enter()
        
        if b == b'\x7f' or b == b'\x08':  # Backspace
            if self.input_text:
                self.input_text = self.input_text[:-1]
                self.needs_rebuild = True
            return None
        
        if b == b'\x03':  # Ctrl-C
            return 'quit'
        
        if b == b'\x04':  # Ctrl-D
            return 'quit'
        
        if b == b'?':
            if not self.input_text and not self.verb_mode:
                self._show_help()
                return None
        
        # Regular characters
        if len(b) == 1:
            c = chr(b[0])
            if c == ' ':
                self.verb_mode = True
                self.input_text = ""
                self.needs_rebuild = False  # Just redraw
                self._redraw()
                return None
            elif c == ':':
                self.verb_mode = True
                self.input_text = ":"
                self.needs_rebuild = False
                self._redraw()
                return None
            elif c.isprintable() or ord(c) > 127:
                if self.verb_mode:
                    self.input_text += c
                    # Check for verb completion
                    verb = self.input_text.lstrip(': ')
                    if verb in ('q', 'quit'):
                        pass  # Will be handled on Enter
                    elif verb in ('pt', 'print_tree'):
                        pass
                else:
                    self.input_text += c
                    self.needs_rebuild = True
                return None
        
        # Multi-byte (UTF-8)
        if len(b) > 1 and b[0] == 0x1b:
            seq = b
            # Alt-Enter
            if seq == b'\x1b\r' or seq == b'\x1b\n':
                selected = self._get_selected_node()
                if selected:
                    return 'open'
            # Alt-h: toggle hidden
            elif seq == b'\x1bh':
                self.show_hidden = not self.show_hidden
                self.needs_rebuild = True
            # Alt-i: toggle git-ignored
            elif seq == b'\x1bi':
                self.show_git_ignored = not self.show_git_ignored
                self.needs_rebuild = True
        
        return None
    
    def _handle_enter(self):
        """Handle Enter key"""
        if self.verb_mode:
            verb = self.input_text.strip().lstrip(': ')
            self.input_text = ""
            self.verb_mode = False
            
            if verb in ('q', 'quit'):
                return 'quit'
            elif verb in ('pt', 'print_tree'):
                return 'print_tree'
            elif verb.startswith('focus '):
                path = verb[6:].strip()
                if path.startswith('~'):
                    path = str(Path.home()) + path[1:]
                new_path = Path(path)
                if new_path.is_dir():
                    self.history.append((self.root_path, self.selected_idx))
                    self.root_path = new_path
                    self.selected_idx = 0
                    self.needs_rebuild = True
            self.needs_rebuild = True
            return None
        
        # Navigate into directory
        selected = self._get_selected_node()
        if selected:
            if selected.is_dir:
                # Go into directory
                self.history.append((self.root_path, self.selected_idx))
                self.root_path = selected.path
                self.selected_idx = 0
                self.input_text = ""
                self.needs_rebuild = True
                return None
            else:
                # Open file or navigate up
                pass
        else:
            # No selection, go up
            parent = self.root_path.parent
            if parent != self.root_path:
                self.history.append((self.root_path, self.selected_idx))
                self.root_path = parent
                self.selected_idx = 0
                self.needs_rebuild = True
        
        return None
    
    def _move_selection(self, delta):
        """Move selection by delta"""
        # Skip root node (index 0)
        selectable = [i for i, (node, _, _) in enumerate(self.flat_nodes) 
                      if i > 0 and node.path is not None]
        
        if not selectable:
            return
        
        if self.selected_idx == 0 and delta > 0:
            self.selected_idx = selectable[0]
            return
        
        try:
            cur_pos = selectable.index(self.selected_idx)
        except ValueError:
            self.selected_idx = selectable[0]
            return
        
        new_pos = max(0, min(len(selectable)-1, cur_pos + delta))
        self.selected_idx = selectable[new_pos]
    
    def _get_selected_node(self):
        """Get the currently selected node"""
        if 0 <= self.selected_idx < len(self.flat_nodes):
            node, _, _ = self.flat_nodes[self.selected_idx]
            return node
        return None
    
    def _show_help(self):
        """Show help screen briefly"""
        pass  # TODO: implement help screen
    
    def _redraw(self):
        """Redraw the entire TUI"""
        h = self.virtual_height
        w = self.width
        
        output = []
        
        # Move to top-left
        output.append(GOTO(1, 1).encode())
        
        tree_height = h - 2
        
        # Draw tree lines
        for row in range(1, tree_height + 1):
            output.append(GOTO(row, 1).encode())
            
            if row == 1:
                # Root line
                if self.colors:
                    output.append((COLOR_ROOT + str(self.root_path) + RESET + 
                                  fg256(254) + bg256(238)).encode())
                else:
                    output.append(str(self.root_path).encode())
                output.append((' ' * max(0, w - len(str(self.root_path)))).encode())
                if self.colors:
                    output.append(RESET.encode())
            else:
                idx = row - 2 + self.scroll_offset  # Index into flat_nodes (skip root)
                if idx < len(self.flat_nodes) - 1:  # -1 because flat_nodes[0] is root
                    node, prefix_stack, is_last = self.flat_nodes[idx + 1]
                    line = self._render_node_line(node, prefix_stack, is_last, 
                                                   idx + 1 == self.selected_idx, w)
                    output.append(line.encode())
                else:
                    # Empty line
                    output.append((' ' * w).encode())
                    if self.colors:
                        output.append(RESET.encode())
        
        # Status bar
        output.append(GOTO(h - 1, 1).encode())
        status = self._get_status_text()
        if self.colors:
            output.append((COLOR_STATUS_BG + COLOR_STATUS_FG + ' ' + status + 
                          ' ' * max(0, w - len(status) - 1) + RESET).encode())
        else:
            output.append((' ' + status + ' ' * max(0, w - len(status) - 1)).encode())
        
        # Input/flags line
        output.append(GOTO(h, 1).encode())
        
        input_display = self.input_text if self.input_text else ""
        flags = self._get_flags_display()
        
        if self.colors:
            cursor = " " if not self.input_text else ""
            input_part = (COLOR_INPUT_BG + COLOR_INPUT_FG + 
                         "\x1b[7m \x1b[0m" +
                         COLOR_INPUT_FG + COLOR_INPUT_BG + 
                         input_display + ' ' * max(0, w - len(flags) - len(input_display) - 1) +
                         RESET)
            flags_part = (COLOR_FLAG_KEY + " h:" + COLOR_FLAG_VAL + 
                         ("y" if self.show_hidden else "n") + RESET +
                         COLOR_FLAG_KEY + "  gi:" + COLOR_FLAG_VAL +
                         ("n" if self.show_git_ignored else "y") + RESET +
                         COLOR_INPUT_BG + " " + RESET)
        else:
            input_part = input_display
            flags_part = f" h:{'y' if self.show_hidden else 'n'}  gi:{'n' if self.show_git_ignored else 'y'}"
        
        output.append((COLOR_INPUT_BG if self.colors else b'').encode() if isinstance(input_part, str) else b'')

        if self.colors:

            h_val = "y" if self.show_hidden else "n"

            flags_str = (f"\x1b[38;5;247m\x1b[48;5;234m h:\x1b[1m\x1b[38;5;178mn\x1b[0m\x1b[38;5;247m\x1b[48;5;234m  gi:\x1b[1m\x1b[38;5;178my\x1b[0m\x1b[38;5;247m\x1b[48;5;234m \x1b[38;5;254m\x1b[49m")

            input_line = (f"\x1b[38;5;231m\x1b[48;5;234m{sel_mark}"

                         f"\x1b[38;5;254m\x1b[49m")
            # Pad and add flags

            flags_visible = f" h:{'y' if self.show_hidden else 'n'}  gi:{'n' if self.show_git_ignored else 'y'} "
            pad = max(0, w - visible_len - len(flags_visible))
            full_line = input_line + " " * pad + flags_str
            output.append(full_line.encode())
        else:
            flags_str = f" h:{'y' if self.show_hidden else 'n'}  gi:{'n' if self.show_git_ignored else 'y'}"
            pad = max(0, w - len(input_display) - len(flags_str))
            output.append((input_display + " " * pad + flags_str).encode())
        
        self.tty_file.write(b''.join(output))
        self.tty_file.flush()
    
    def _render_node_line(self, node, prefix_stack, is_last, selected, width):
        """Render a single tree node line"""
        prefix = ""
        for has_more in prefix_stack:
            prefix += VERT_CONT if has_more else INDENT
        
        branch = BRANCH_LAST if is_last else BRANCH_MID
        
        if node.path is None:
            name = node.name + " "
        elif node.is_dir and node.collapsed and not node.children:
            name = node.name + f" {ELLIPSIS} "
        else:
            name = node.name + " "
        
        # Selection marker
        sel_mark = "\u25b6" if selected else " "
        
        full = f"{sel_mark}{prefix}{branch}{name}"
        
        # Pad to width
        # Calculate visible length (approximate, ignoring color codes)
        visible_len = len(full)
        pad = max(0, width - visible_len)
        
        if self.colors:
            if selected:
                return (COLOR_SELECT_MARK + sel_mark + RESET +
                        COLOR_TREE_CHARS + prefix + branch + RESET +
                        (COLOR_DIR if (node.is_dir and node.path) else COLOR_FILE) +
                        name + RESET +
                        " " * pad)
            else:
                if node.path is None:
                    return (" " + COLOR_TREE_CHARS + prefix + branch + RESET +
                            COLOR_UNLISTED + name + RESET + " " * pad)
                return (" " + COLOR_TREE_CHARS + prefix + branch + RESET +
                        (COLOR_DIR if node.is_dir else COLOR_FILE) +
                        name + RESET + " " * pad)
        else:
            return full + " " * pad
    
    def _get_status_text(self):
        """Get the status bar text"""
        if self.verb_mode:
            return "Type a verb then enter to execute it (? for the list of verbs)"
        
        if self.input_text:
            selected = self._get_selected_node()
            if selected and selected.is_dir:
                return "Hit enter to focus, ? for help, or a space then a verb"
            return "Hit alt-Enter to open and quit, esc to clear the filter, ? for help, or a space then a verb"
        
        selected = self._get_selected_node()
        if selected:
            if selected.is_dir:
                return "Hit enter to focus, ? for help, or a space then a verb"
            return "Hit enter to open, ? for help, or a space then a verb"
        
        if self.history:
            return "Hit esc to go back, enter to go up, ? for help, or a few letters to search"
        
        return "Hit enter to go up, ? for help, or a few letters to search"
    
    def _get_flags_display(self):
        """Get the flags display string"""
        h_val = "y" if self.show_hidden else "n"
        gi_val = "n" if self.show_git_ignored else "y"
        return f"h:{h_val}  gi:{gi_val}"

# ── File system tree ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
class FileNode:
    __slots__ = ['name', 'path', 'is_dir', 'children', 'parent', 'depth',
                 'is_link', 'is_hidden', 'unlisted_count', 'collapsed']
    
    def __init__(self, path, parent=None, depth=0):
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.name = self.path.name
        self.parent = parent
        self.depth = depth
        self.children = []
        self.unlisted_count = 0
        self.collapsed = False  # True means show "…" (no expansion at all)
        
        try:
            st = self.path.lstat()
            self.is_link = stat.S_ISLNK(st.st_mode)
            if self.is_link:
                try:
                    st2 = self.path.stat()
                    self.is_dir = stat.S_ISDIR(st2.st_mode)
                except OSError:
                    self.is_dir = False
            else:
                self.is_dir = stat.S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)
        except OSError:
            self.is_dir = False
            self.is_link = False
        
        self.is_hidden = self.name.startswith('.')

def _get_children(dirpath, show_hidden=False, show_git_ignored=True,
                  only_folders=False, pattern=None, depth=0, max_depth=None):
    """Get sorted children of a directory"""
    try:
        entries = list(os.scandir(dirpath))
    except PermissionError:
        return []
    
    result = []
    for entry in entries:
        name = entry.name
        if not show_hidden and name.startswith('.'):
            continue
        try:
            is_dir = entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=True)
        except OSError:
            is_dir = False
        
        if only_folders and not is_dir:
            continue
        
        result.append(entry)
    
    # Sort case-insensitively
    result.sort(key=lambda e: e.name.lower())
    return result

# ── Tree building and pruning ────────────────────────────────────────────────
class Tree:
    def __init__(self, root_path, opts):
        self.root_path = Path(root_path).resolve()
        self.opts = opts
        self.nodes = []  # Flat list of visible nodes (for display)
        self.selected_idx = 0
        self.scroll_offset = 0
        self.pattern = ""
        self.pattern_type = "fuzzy"  # fuzzy, exact, regex
        self.search_results = []
        
    def build(self, available_lines):
        """Build the tree fitting in available_lines (including root line)"""
        self.nodes = []
        if available_lines <= 0:
            available_lines = 1
        
        # Always show root
        root_node = FileNode(self.root_path)
        root_node.depth = 0
        
        if available_lines == 1:
            self.nodes = [root_node]
            return
        
        # Get children recursively with pruning
        item_budget = available_lines - 1  # Lines available for items (not root)
        children = self._build_tree_nodes(self.root_path, 0, item_budget)
        self.nodes = [root_node] + children
    
    def _build_tree_nodes(self, dirpath, depth, budget):
        """Recursively build tree nodes fitting in budget lines"""
        if budget <= 0:
            return []
        
        opts = self.opts
        entries = _get_children(
            dirpath,
            show_hidden=opts.get('hidden', False),
            only_folders=opts.get('only_folders', False),
        )
        
        if not entries:
            return []
        
        # Apply pattern filter if set
        if self.pattern and depth > 0:
            # When searching, show full paths for matches
            pass
        
        max_depth = opts.get('max_depth')
        if max_depth is not None and depth >= max_depth:
            # At max depth, just show items without expanding dirs
            nodes = []
            for entry in entries:
                if len(nodes) >= budget:
                    break
                node = FileNode(entry.path, depth=depth+1)
                node.collapsed = node.is_dir
                nodes.append(node)
            return nodes
        
        # Calculate how many entries we can show
        # For each entry: needs 1 line minimum
        # For each dir that can be expanded: needs extra lines for children
        
        nodes = self._allocate_budget(dirpath, entries, depth, budget)
        return nodes
    
    def _allocate_budget(self, dirpath, entries, depth, budget):
        """Allocate budget across entries, expanding dirs as allowed"""
        if not entries:
            return []
        
        n = len(entries)
        
        # First pass: if all entries fit with collapsed dirs
        if n <= budget:
            # We have room. Now try to expand dirs.
            nodes = []
            remaining = budget - n  # Extra lines after showing all entries flat
            
            for i, entry in enumerate(entries):
                is_last = (i == n - 1)
                node = FileNode(entry.path, depth=depth+1)
                
                if node.is_dir and remaining > 0:
                    # Try to expand this directory
                    sub_entries = _get_children(
                        entry.path,
                        show_hidden=self.opts.get('hidden', False),
                        only_folders=self.opts.get('only_folders', False),
                    )
                    
                    if sub_entries:
                        # We need at least 1 extra line for the first child or unlisted
                        available_for_children = remaining
                        if available_for_children > 0:
                            children = self._allocate_budget(
                                entry.path, sub_entries, depth+1, available_for_children
                            )
                            if children:
                                used = sum(1 for _ in self._count_nodes(children))
                                remaining -= used
                                node.children = children
                
                nodes.append(node)
            return nodes
        else:
            # More entries than budget: show as many as fit, last is "unlisted"
            shown = []
            
            if budget <= 0:
                return []
            
            # Show budget-1 entries, then add unlisted count
            show_count = budget - 1  # Reserve 1 for "N unlisted"
            if show_count <= 0:
                # Can't show anything meaningful
                # Show "N unlisted" as the only item
                unlisted_node = _make_unlisted_node(n, depth+1)
                return [unlisted_node]
            
            for entry in entries[:show_count]:
                node = FileNode(entry.path, depth=depth+1)
                node.collapsed = True  # Show with "…" since no room to expand
                shown.append(node)
            
            unlisted_count = n - show_count
            if unlisted_count > 0:
                shown.append(_make_unlisted_node(unlisted_count, depth+1))
            
            return shown
    
    def _count_nodes(self, nodes):
        """Yield all nodes recursively"""
        for node in nodes:
            yield node
            if node.children:
                yield from self._count_nodes(node.children)

def _make_unlisted_node(count, depth):
    """Create a synthetic 'N unlisted' node"""
    node = FileNode.__new__(FileNode)
    node.name = f"{count} unlisted"
    node.path = None
    node.is_dir = False
    node.is_link = False
    node.is_hidden = False
    node.parent = None
    node.depth = depth
    node.children = []
    node.unlisted_count = count
    node.collapsed = False
    return node

def render_tree_to_lines(root_path, available_lines, opts):
    """
    Render a directory tree and return list of (line_str, is_item) tuples.
    available_lines = total output lines (including root line).
    Returns list of strings with CRLF endings.
    """
    root_path = Path(root_path).resolve()
    lines = []
    
    # Add root line
    lines.append(str(root_path) + "\r\n")
    
    item_budget = available_lines - 1
    if item_budget <= 0:
        return lines
    
    # Build the tree
    tree = Tree(root_path, opts)
    tree.build(available_lines)
    
    # Render nodes (skip root node which is already added)
    nodes = tree.nodes[1:]  # Skip root
    
    # Flatten to display list with prefix info
    flat = []
    _flatten_nodes(nodes, [], flat)
    
    for prefix, node, is_last in flat:
        if len(lines) >= available_lines:
            break
        branch = BRANCH_LAST if is_last else BRANCH_MID
        
        if node.path is None:
            # Unlisted node
            name_str = f"{node.name} "
            line = f" {prefix}{branch}{name_str}\r\n"
        elif node.is_dir and node.collapsed and not node.children:
            # Directory shown with ellipsis
            line = f" {prefix}{branch}{node.name} {ELLIPSIS} \r\n"
        else:
            name_str = node.name + " "
            line = f" {prefix}{branch}{name_str}\r\n"
        
        lines.append(line)
    
    return lines

def _flatten_nodes(nodes, parent_has_more_stack, result):
    """Flatten node tree to list with prefix info"""
    for i, node in enumerate(nodes):
        is_last = (i == len(nodes) - 1)
        
        # Build prefix from stack
        prefix = ""
        for has_more in parent_has_more_stack:
            prefix += VERT_CONT if has_more else INDENT
        
        result.append((prefix, node, is_last))
        
        if node.children:
            new_stack = parent_has_more_stack + [not is_last]
            _flatten_nodes(node.children, new_stack, result)

def parse_args(argv):
    args = Args()
    i = 1
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        
        # Long options with values
        def get_val(opt_str):
            nonlocal i
            if '=' in opt_str:
                return opt_str.split('=', 1)[1]
            i += 1
            if i >= len(argv):
                print(f"error: missing value for {opt_str}", file=sys.stderr)
                sys.exit(1)
            return argv[i]
        
        if arg in ('--version', '-V'):
            args.version = True
        elif arg == '--help':
            args.help = True
        elif arg.startswith('--cmd=') or (arg == '--cmd' or arg == '-c'):
            if arg == '--cmd' or arg == '-c':
                args.cmd = get_val(arg)
            else:
                args.cmd = arg[6:]
        elif arg.startswith('-c='):
            args.cmd = arg[3:]
        elif arg.startswith('--color='):
            args.color = arg[8:]
        elif arg == '--color':
            args.color = get_val(arg)
        elif arg.startswith('--height='):
            args.height = int(arg[9:])
        elif arg == '--height':
            args.height = int(get_val(arg))
        elif arg in ('--hidden', '-h'):
            args.hidden = True
        elif arg in ('--no-hidden', '-H'):
            args.no_hidden = True
        elif arg in ('--git-ignored', '-i'):
            args.git_ignored = True
        elif arg in ('--no-git-ignored', '-I'):
            args.no_git_ignored = True
        elif arg in ('--show-git-info', '-g'):
            args.show_git_info = True
        elif arg in ('--no-show-git-info', '-G'):
            args.no_show_git_info = True
        elif arg in ('--only-folders', '-f'):
            args.only_folders = True
        elif arg in ('--no-only-folders', '-F'):
            args.no_only_folders = True
        elif arg in ('--sizes', '-s'):
            args.sizes = True
        elif arg in ('--no-sizes', '-S'):
            args.no_sizes = True
        elif arg in ('--dates', '-d'):
            args.dates = True
        elif arg in ('--no-dates', '-D'):
            args.no_dates = True
        elif arg in ('--permissions', '-p'):
            args.permissions = True
        elif arg in ('--no-permissions', '-P'):
            args.no_permissions = True
        elif arg == '--sort-by-count':
            args.sort_by_count = True
        elif arg == '--sort-by-date':
            args.sort_by_date = True
        elif arg == '--sort-by-size':
            args.sort_by_size = True
        elif arg == '--sort-by-type':
            args.sort_by_type = True
        elif arg == '--sort-by-type-dirs-first':
            args.sort_by_type_dirs_first = True
        elif arg == '--sort-by-type-dirs-last':
            args.sort_by_type_dirs_last = True
        elif arg == '--no-sort':
            args.no_sort = True
        elif arg in ('--whale-spotting', '-w'):
            args.whale_spotting = True
        elif arg in ('--trim-root', '-t'):
            args.trim_root = True
        elif arg in ('--no-trim-root', '-T'):
            args.no_trim_root = True
        elif arg == '--show-root-fs':
            args.show_root_fs = True
        elif arg == '--git-status':
            args.git_status = True
        elif arg == '--tree':
            args.tree = True
        elif arg == '--no-tree':
            args.no_tree = True
        elif arg.startswith('--max-depth='):
            args.max_depth = int(arg[12:])
        elif arg == '--max-depth':
            args.max_depth = int(get_val(arg))
        elif arg.startswith('--outcmd='):
            args.outcmd = arg[9:]
        elif arg == '--outcmd':
            args.outcmd = get_val(arg)
        elif arg.startswith('--conf='):
            args.conf = arg[7:]
        elif arg == '--conf':
            args.conf = get_val(arg)
        elif arg == '--install':
            args.install = True
        elif arg.startswith('--set-install-state='):
            args.set_install_state = arg[20:]
        elif arg == '--set-install-state':
            args.set_install_state = get_val(arg)
        elif arg.startswith('--print-shell-function='):
            args.print_shell_function = arg[23:]
        elif arg == '--print-shell-function':
            args.print_shell_function = get_val(arg)
        elif arg.startswith('--listen='):
            args.listen = arg[9:]
        elif arg == '--listen':
            args.listen = get_val(arg)
        elif arg == '--listen-auto':
            args.listen_auto = True
        elif arg == '--get-root':
            args.get_root = True
        elif arg.startswith('--write-default-conf='):
            args.write_default_conf = arg[21:]
        elif arg == '--write-default-conf':
            args.write_default_conf = get_val(arg)
        elif arg.startswith('--send='):
            args.send = arg[7:]
        elif arg == '--send':
            args.send = get_val(arg)
        elif arg.startswith('--verb-output='):
            args.verb_output = arg[14:]
        elif arg == '--verb-output':
            args.verb_output = get_val(arg)
        elif arg == '--':
            i += 1
            if i < len(argv):
                args.root = argv[i]
            break
        elif arg.startswith('-') and len(arg) > 1:
            # Possibly combined short flags like -sdp
            # Try to parse each char
            j = 1
            while j < len(arg):
                c = arg[j]
                if c == 's': args.sizes = True
                elif c == 'S': args.no_sizes = True
                elif c == 'd': args.dates = True
                elif c == 'D': args.no_dates = True
                elif c == 'p': args.permissions = True
                elif c == 'P': args.no_permissions = True
                elif c == 'h': args.hidden = True
                elif c == 'H': args.no_hidden = True
                elif c == 'i': args.git_ignored = True
                elif c == 'I': args.no_git_ignored = True
                elif c == 'g': args.show_git_info = True
                elif c == 'G': args.no_show_git_info = True
                elif c == 'f': args.only_folders = True
                elif c == 'F': args.no_only_folders = True
                elif c == 'w': args.whale_spotting = True
                elif c == 't': args.trim_root = True
                elif c == 'T': args.no_trim_root = True
                elif c == 'V': args.version = True
                elif c == 'c':
                    # -c needs value
                    if j + 1 < len(arg):
                        args.cmd = arg[j+1:]
                    else:
                        i += 1
                        args.cmd = argv[i] if i < len(argv) else ""
                    break
                j += 1
        else:
            # Positional argument = root path
            args.root = arg
        
        i += 1
    
    # whale-spotting implies hidden and git-ignored
    if args.whale_spotting:
        args.hidden = True
        args.git_ignored = True
        if not args.sort_by_size:
            args.sort_by_size = True
    
    return args
